crime_highlights: Approximately 4,200 marihuana plants in various stages of growth were found on the property.

The sentencing judge concluded the appellant used licences authorizing the production of a relatively small number of marihuana plants for personal medical use as a veil of legitimacy in order to avoid detection of the larger illegal enterprise with which he was involved.
The sentencing judge concluded that the grow operation had the capacity to generate significant revenue.
rationale_highlights: a number of adverse factors that affect Indigenous people generally are present in the appellant's life
the judge considered the information contained in the Gladue report as providing necessary context to determine an appropriate sentence in this case
The judge determined that the appellant's moral culpability was high.
note: Court never says Gladue reduced culpability; judge found culpability high; drug case, no victim harm.

He produced a 10-inch knife and held it against her throat.
the appellant attacked her with the knife

rationale_highlights: His parents and grandparents were survivors of the residential school system.

Mr. Awasis' experiences as an Aboriginal person have contributed to his present personality and tendencies such that he must by law be considered to be less morally blameworthy for his criminal acts than if he did not have those antecedents
the judge accepted that the appellant's Gladue factors reduced his moral blameworthiness
note: Dangerous offender; reduced blameworthiness accepted but public protection paramount.

crime_highlights: Mr. Hiscock fired at least seven shots
Three of the shots struck an unoccupied car parked in front of the residence.
Other bullets penetrated the interior walls of the residence and damaged fixtures and property.
rationale_highlights: it is the sort of connection between Mr. Hiscock's present circumstances and his Aboriginal status that calls for overt consideration of his moral blameworthiness
the reasons for sentence do not give tangible effect to the serious systemic issues and background factors noted in the Gladue report that are applicable to Mr. Hiscock's life
his background must have a mitigating effect upon sentence
note: Offence has no human victim; harm limited to property damage and danger.
